sections.title: Principios

summary.text: Sets out the principles of the Pandemic Influenza Preparedness Framework, in which WHO Member States recall earlier resolutions and note the ongoing risk of an influenza pandemic. They affirm the importance of rapid, systematic sharing of viruses alongside fair and equitable sharing of benefits. They also stress sovereign rights over biological resources and equitable access to quality vaccines, medicines and technologies for developing countries.

sections.title: Objetivo

summary.text: States the Framework's objective of improving pandemic influenza preparedness and response through a fair, transparent and efficient WHO global influenza surveillance and response system, putting virus sharing and benefit sharing on an equal footing.

sections.extract: 2. sections.title: Alcance

summary.text: Defines the Framework's scope as covering the sharing of H5N1 and other potentially pandemic human influenza viruses and related benefits, but not seasonal influenza or other pathogens.

sections.extract: 3. Alcance 3.1 Este Marco se aplica al intercambio de virus H5N1 y otros virus gripales poten- cialmente pandémicos para el hombre y la compartición de los beneficios deri- vados de su uso. 3.2 Este Marco no se aplica a los virus de la gripe estacional ni a otros agentes patógenos o sustancias biológicas no gripales que puedan contener las mues- tras clínicas intercambiadas de conformidad con el presente Marco.

sections.title: Definiciones y uso de los términos

summary.text: Introduces the definitions of terms used in the Framework.

sections.extract: 4. Definiciones y uso de los términos Para los efectos del presente Marco, los términos siguientes tienen el significado que se les asigna a continuación.

sections.title: Materiales biológicos de preparación para una gripe pandémica o «Materiales biológicos PIP»

summary.text: Defines "PIP biological materials" as human clinical specimens, virus isolates of wild-type H5N1 and other potentially pandemic influenza viruses, modified viruses and related genetic material covered by the Framework and its transfer agreements.

sections.title: Otros términos técnicos

summary.text: Defines further technical terms used in the Framework, such as genetic sequences, reference reagents and diagnostic reagents. It also defines candidate vaccine viruses and related materials. Wild-type viruses are defined as those grown directly from clinical specimens without deliberate modification.

sections.extract: «Secuencias genéticas»: orden en que aparecen los nucleótidos en una molécu- la de ADN o ARN. Contienen la información genética que determina las carac- terísticas biológicas de un organismo o virus. «Reactivos de referencia»: sustancias biológicas o químicas u organismos o partes de los mismos empleados en las actividades de diagnóstico o vigilancia. summary.text: Defines the laboratories in the WHO global influenza surveillance and response system, including Essential Regulatory Laboratories, National Influenza Centres, WHO Collaborating Centres and H5 Reference Laboratories. It also defines other institutions and entities such as vaccine manufacturers.

sections.title: Consideraciones generales

summary.text: Sets out general provisions for virus sharing, asking Member States, through National Influenza Centres and authorized laboratories, to send PIP biological materials from all human cases of H5N1 and other potentially pandemic viruses to WHO laboratories promptly. It describes the consent and conditions for onward transfer under the Framework.

summary.text: Provides that genetic sequence data on H5N1 and other potentially pandemic viruses should be shared rapidly with the originating laboratory and among WHO surveillance laboratories. It encourages greater transparency in making such data available.

summary.text: Commits the Director-General to establish a WHO stockpile of H5N1 and other potentially pandemic vaccines with related equipment, initially 150 million doses, used on expert advice. It covers deployment plans developed with experts and Member States.

summary.text: Calls on Member States to urge manufacturers to set aside part of each production run of potentially pandemic vaccines for developing countries during inter-pandemic periods. These supplies should be available at the same time as for developed countries and at tiered prices.

summary.text: Urges influenza vaccine and antiviral manufacturers to apply tiered pricing so that developing countries can afford pandemic vaccines and antivirals, taking account of the vulnerability of least developed countries.

summary.text: Sets out sustainable and innovative financing for the benefit-sharing system, including an annual partnership contribution from influenza vaccine, diagnostic and pharmaceutical manufacturers using the WHO system. It explains how the contribution is set relative to the system's running costs, around half of them. It describes how the funds will be used for pandemic preparedness and response.

summary.text: Provides that the World Health Assembly oversees implementation of the Framework with advice from the Director-General. The oversight mechanism includes an independent Advisory Group with regional and expert representation.

summary.text: Requires the Director-General to report every two years to the Health Assembly on laboratory and surveillance capacity, vaccine production capacity, transfer agreements and benefit sharing. The Framework is to be reviewed in 2016 with proposed revisions in 2017.

sections.title: Anexos

summary.text: Contains the annexes of the Framework, starting with Standard Material Transfer Agreement 1 for transfers of PIP biological materials within the WHO global influenza surveillance and response system. It sets out the terms binding providers and recipients, followed by Standard Material Transfer Agreement 2 for recipients outside the system, with their benefit-sharing commitments. Further annexes give the Advisory Group's terms of reference and its procedures. The block ends with the heading of Annex 4 on guiding principles for terms of reference of the system's laboratories.

sections.title: Anexo 5 Mandato relativo al trabajo con materiales biológicos de preparación para una gripe pandémica

summary.text: Annex 5 gives terms of reference for laboratories working with PIP biological materials, starting with background on the WHO global influenza surveillance and response system as an alert mechanism for viruses of pandemic potential. It covers the four categories of laboratories in turn, beginning with WHO Collaborating Centres on influenza. It sets out their duties on virus receipt, characterization, sharing, publication and acknowledgement of originating laboratories. It closes with the ISBN and WHO's address.
